rv.q: Happily, though, American Blues Theater’s production of “Always … Patsy Cline,” Ted Swindley’s warhorse of a revue that premiered in 1988, largely won me over with the warmth of its two leading ladies — Liz Chidester and Molly Hernández — and its tender portrayal of their unexpected friendship.
American Blues Theater has done it again with Always…Patsy Cline, running now through June 21st.
For a cool two hours of pure joy and entertainment, we’re back in the late 1950’s-early 60’s, snuggling comfortably and “Back in Baby’s Arms” once more.
The 1988 tuner is a boot-scooting, twangtacular delight defined by lush vocals and high-octane energy.
Always…Patsy Cline hits every banger in her juke box for a sonically charged good time that will make you want to leave your seat and Texas two-step down the aisle.

If you’re like me, you’ll relish the music but go away a bit disappointed that a show ostensibly about Patsy Cline tells us so little about her—i.e., that it treats her as an icon, not a flesh-and-blood human being.
This production not only gives the audience the opportunity to reminisce about Patsy and her bold singing voice but also to learn something about her life.

cn.t: Critics praise this crowd-pleasing jukebox musical for Liz Chidester's terrific star turn as Patsy Cline and its irresistible score of emotionally rich hits, calling it a joyous journey through the country legend's music and friendship story.
